newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac Australia March leading index falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac Australia March leading index falls.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index of Australian economic activity, which measures where activity will be in six to nine months time, fell 2.3 points or 1.4 percent in March.
The coincident index, which provides a broad measure of the current state of economic activity, fell by one point or 0.7 percent in March.

"The fall in the leading index is mainly explained by the sharp fall in the volatile series for non-residential private building approvals to levels well below recent trend," Westpac general manager, economics, Bill Evans said in a statement.
"We expect there will be a sharp rebound in that series over the next few months returning the leading index to the positive upward growth trend of the last six months," Evans said.
Evans noted that the fall in the leading index had pulled the annual growth rate of the series down to 2.2 percent in March from 5.4 percent in February.
He also said that the slight fall in the coincident index reflected the fall in retail trade and employment growth which were partially offset by a small reduction in the rate of unemployment.
"The leading index for all countries has picked up to an annual growth rate of 6.5 percent, which is sending a clear message that world growth is going to be much stronger by late 1997," Evans said.

"That will be very good news for Australian exporters and, given exports of goods and services account for 25 percent of Australia's output, this is welcome prospect for the economy as a whole," Evans added.
The leading index of inflation fell slightly to 4.3 percent in March, continuing to suggest moderation in inflation pressures.
